newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: VODACOM BUYS EXTRA 10 PCT OF TELJOY.
newsitem.headline: VODACOM BUYS EXTRA 10 PCT OF TELJOY.

text.p: Teljoy Holdings Ltd said on Monday it had sold a further 10 percent of Teljoy Cellular Services to Vodacom, the joint venture network operator owned by Britain's Vodafone Plc and state-run Telkom SA.
The acquisition, for approximately 20 million rand in cash, is effective September 30, 1996.
The deal lifts Vodacom's stake to 35 percent and reduces Teljoy's to 65 percent.

Teljoy Cellular has also repaid loans of 50 million rand to its shareholders, Teljoy Holdings and Vodacom, in the ratio 75:25. This emanates from previous surplus funding and improved cash flows over the last few months.
The combined inflow of some 58 million to Teljoy Holdings will substantially improve the balance sheet and result in a major repayment of bank loans, the company said.
Teljoy chief executive Johann Pieterse said gearing would fall to acceptable levels, completing a capital restructure of Teljoy Holdings.
"Teljoy Holdings will therefore not require a capital increase or restructuring in the foreseeable future," the company said in a statement.
Pieterse said attention was now being turned to Teljoy Television Services which has been hit by disappointing demand for satellite televisions and is also being restructured.
Chief operating officer Jon Stoffberg has resigned and Harry Potgieter, a former director of Teljoy Holdings, has been contracted indefinitely to assist in refocusing the TV division.
Further details would be provided with interim results in November, Pieterse said.
